title: ConflictEvent — the ~300 byte record
description: Produced by M3 (owner B), emitted by edge/emit, ingested by M7 (owner D). Parent PRD 5.3, as amended by edge PRD A3. Serialised form MUST be <= 400 bytes.

event_id.description: evt_<8 hex>, a deterministic hash of video_id + unordered track pair + min_ttc_frame. Ingest is idempotent on this field, so it must be stable across re-runs and buffer replays.

time.description: Wall-clock ISO-8601, derived from the configured video start time plus t_video_s. Never mixed with t_video_s.

ttc_s.description: Minimum time-to-collision observed across the encounter, on the ground plane. Never pixel space.

pet_s.description: Post-encroachment time. Null when not computed or no path crossing exists — PET is the first thing cut.

severity.description: DERIVED, never hand-set. ttc_s < 0.8 -> severe, ttc_s < 1.5 -> conflict. Parent PRD 5.3 hard rule.

conditions.description: WRITTEN ONLY BY THE SERVER (M6, owner D). The edge always writes null. A populated value arriving from the edge is a bug.

detection_quality.description: Mean detector confidence across both tracks over the encounter. Carried so D can normalise conflict rates by it — detection degrades in rain and darkness, and ignoring that leads to concluding rain is safe.

t_video_s.description: AMENDMENT A3. Seconds from video start at minimum TTC. Lets C align an event to a hand-written label without guessing.

min_ttc_frame.description: AMENDMENT A3. Frame index at which ttc_s was observed.

direction.description: OMITTED BY THE EDGE, added by D on ingest. 'against flow' requires C's learned lane directions (M5); the edge has no lane map and does not write fields it cannot compute. Emitting it as an explicit null cost 38 bytes of the 400-byte budget to say nothing, and pushed the worst-case event to 412 bytes.

$comment: There is NO blame or fault field, and none may be added. We describe what happened; we do not assign responsibility, because we cannot verify it and being wrong harms a real person.
